course_description: This course deals with the introduction to digital hardware design. Combinational and sequential logic circuits are treated. Designing circuits using encoders, decoders, multiplexers, and different types of flip- flops is done for the first part of the course; and then algorithmic state machines are discussed. It also includes concepts relating to computer organization and architecture; instruction set and assembly language; hardware system, central processing unit, and its control; and input-output system and system memory.

identify the fundamental circuit components and techniques for optimizing circuits;
use Boolean algebra as related to designing computer logic, including solving Karnaugh maps;
evaluate the importance of various theories and principles in solving real-life problems by inculcating the usefulness of computer organization;

assess computer organization, structure, characteristics, basic theories of the CPU, memory, and I/O peripherals, the operation of modern day computer systems and the fundamental principles that drive computer designer in designing new architectures; and
